name: The Gorton household at 2120 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_gorton_frank_s

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2120 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903); the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904) prints nothing at 2120. The household left within that year, and whether it was still in the house on 1 July 1904 is not documented.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2120. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. In 1900 the line at this number names Frank S. Gorton with his office and another town written in, and no household. The census says nothing about this household's staff. The 1910 census was not read. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

born.note: Biographical date from the cited period publication(s). The publication date is not the date the photograph was taken.

portrait.caption: Frank S. Gorton, undated photograph published in Men of Illinois (1902), p. 134.
portrait.why: Identified by the printed caption and checked against the household record. The monochrome photograph does not establish skin, eye or clothing colours.

portrait_research.note: An individual portrait has not yet been verified in the period portrait books and Glessner House Museum article archive searched for this project. Any figure shown is a reconstruction, not an attested likeness.
